title: Studies and Students, and Remembering Vaastu Devtas
sub: Complete notes on Jyotish Vidya Ep. 11 by Brajesh Gautam, The Anchor Of Life. Why a bright child's marks can fall, why not to punish a struggling child, exam-day colour and thread remedies, a sketch of the vastu deities, and why no single chart is read alone.
desc: Complete notes on Jyotish Vidya Ep. 11, Studies and Students and Remembering Vaastu Devtas by Brajesh Gautam: planetary causes of study trouble, exam-day remedies, picking the right deity, a vastu overview and a remedy cheat sheet, with video timestamps.
points: Marks can fall after age 10 for planetary reasons.
A combust or retrograde Mercury or Jupiter is his usual explanation, not laziness.
Do not punish a struggling child.
A rude tone, refusal to listen, mood swings or superstition are read as planetary faults, not character.
A failed exam can be the cheaper outcome.
A lost fee or a repeated year is treated as a cheaper payment than a health problem later.
Match the deity to the chart.
The commonly named deity is not always the right one for a specific child's placement.
Exam-day colours and threads are specific, not universal.
What helps one child's chart can hurt another's; this page keeps his examples as illustrations only.
No single chart is read alone.
Near a sign's edge, the chalit, nirayana and KP charts can each shift a planet into a different house.
A well-fitted stone is treated as good for about a hundred years, not replaced every few.
